decisions.title: What quorum should apply during the pilot?

options.text: No quorum: every ballot counts however many vote. The host asked if anyone objected to this for the next four weeks and heard no objection (00:35:28).
A minimum of 20 votes: simple to check; 24 people voted on the 16 November ballot.
25% of the voting body: Joel Okomoli’s view (00:36:09). The host estimated a hundred and something contributors and co-editors, so about 25 to 30 votes (00:34:52).
options.label: Participant proposal

options.text: 25% of the active voting body: the host’s suggestion (00:37:04). It needs a definition of “active” first.
options.label: Participant proposal

options.text: The 16 November vote tied 6 to 6 between a minimum of 20 votes and 25% of the voting body (no quorum: 5).

decisions.raisedBy: Raised by: Daveed Benjamin (00:31:25, 00:35:28). 25% supported by Joel Okomoli (00:36:09). Related: question 5 of the 16 November ballot.

decisions.title: Should an option need a second before it goes into the draft ballot?

options.text: Yes: an option is added to the draft ballot only when another participant seconds it. Fewer stray options, but a lone idea may be dropped.
No: every option raised goes into the draft ballot, as now.

decisions.raisedBy: Suggested by Markabadi in his 20 November walk-through; presented by Daveed Benjamin (00:53:29). Supported by Laura Del Campo (00:55:20) and Leandra Preston (00:55:39).

decisions.title: Should draft ballot options be written in plain English first?

options.text: Yes: the draft states each option in plain English before any formal wording is settled.
No: draft directly in formal ballot wording.

decisions.raisedBy: Suggested by Markabadi; presented by Daveed Benjamin (00:55:58). Not discussed.

decisions.title: Should each session open with an optional 30-second check-in?

options.text: Yes: near the start, anyone who wants to says in 30 seconds what is going on for them.
No: keep the current opening.

decisions.raisedBy: Suggested by Markabadi; presented by Daveed Benjamin (00:55:58). Not discussed.

decisions.title: Should each session focus on one major inquiry?

options.text: Yes: one main question per session.
No: keep several topics per session.
Note for the host: you said this needs clarification from Markabadi (00:55:58). It may be better held back until it is clarified.

decisions.raisedBy: Suggested by Markabadi; presented by Daveed Benjamin (00:55:58). Not discussed.

decisions.title: Should Deepi raise its hand when it has something to add?

options.text: Yes: the meeting assistant raises its hand in Zoom when it notices a pattern or something the discussion is missing, and speaks when called on.
No: Deepi answers only when asked.

decisions.raisedBy: Suggested by Markabadi; presented by Daveed Benjamin (00:55:58). Not discussed.

decisions.title: Should the Desirable Properties use opt-in text reminders?

options.text: Yes: people who opt in get a text when review opens and closes and when voting opens and closes (three or four a week), skipping people who have already voted.
No: email reminders only.

decisions.raisedBy: Suggested by Markabadi; presented by Daveed Benjamin, who is building it for the whole estate and said the community can vote on using it here (00:58:17).

decisions.title: Should session transcripts be published on the session page and kept?

options.text: Yes: the transcript is published on the session page and kept, after a 48-hour period for corrections (00:48:24).
No: keep transcripts out of the public page.
Only Laura Del Campo answered, in favour (00:49:15). How long transcripts are kept and who can read them are still open.

decisions.title: After the front matter, how should the book club choose what to read?

options.text: In book order, from DP1 onward: everyone knows what comes next.
Chapters the group picks by interest or background, so people can research and specialize (Joel Okomoli, 01:14:01).
options.label: Participant proposal

options.text: Note for the host: the meeting agreed to put the book club cadence on next week’s agenda (01:14:38), so this may be settled in the room on 30 November rather than by ballot.

decisions.raisedBy: Raised by: Joel Okomoli (01:14:01). Proposed for next week’s agenda by Daveed Benjamin and seconded by Joel Okomoli (01:14:45).

Question 1: you asked whether anyone objected to no quorum and heard none (00:35:28), then Joel Okomoli spoke for 25% and you deferred (00:37:04). If you count the consent call as a decision, drop question 1. “Active voting body” needs a definition before the vote.

Question 1: while reading results you said the tie was with “no quorum” (00:33:11); the published tally has the tie between a minimum of 20 votes and 25%. The transcript keeps what you said, with the tally in brackets.
Questions 3 to 6 were presented but not discussed; only seconding (question 2) drew responses. Multi-select voting was left out as a question: you said “we can handle that” (00:55:58).

Speakers: two participants at 00:13:01 and 00:15:27 (before Deepi rejoined) are not identified. Leandra Preston is a likely candidate for one of them: at 00:21:08 you asked whether her hand was “back up”.

Deepi’s seconded list records Joel Okomoli’s +1 in the chat for seconding and names Daveed Benjamin as the seconder of the book club cadence item; the transcript has Joel Okomoli saying “I second that” after you proposed it (01:14:45).
